verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's own SDKs serve non-boolean values: the quickstart shows `useFeatureValue("button-color", "blue")` returning a string, and the JS SDK documents `getFeatureValue` alongside `isOn`. Rules can force or roll out values that override a feature's default, and experiment rules assign users to one of several variations. However, the pack never explicitly documents number or JSON value types, and the runtime probe exercised only a boolean flag. missing for 10: explicit documentation of number and JSON feature value types, documentation of multivariate (more than two variation) value serving, hands-on or independent corroboration of non-boolean value delivery.

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve multivariate flags and dynamic configuration values (strings, numbers, JSON), not just booleans

citations.quote: There are 2 main methods for evaluating features: `isOn` and `getFeatureValue`
Layer multiple rules on one feature to compose behavior — for example, a forced value for beta testers above a gradual rollout to everyone else.
you can add an experiment rule to a feature that will randomly assign the users based on some hashing attribute into one of your experiment variations.
